subject: Post-call: model fit & evaluation plan for PayGrid
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Khan <samir@paygrid.com>, Laura Chen <laura.chen@paygrid.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 15 Feb 2026 10:12:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call: model fit & evaluation plan for PayGrid

Hi Samir / Laura —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum:

Recap
- Goal: Replace PayGrid's current proprietary NLU baseline in transaction routing & compliance classification with a lower-cost open model stack while maintaining >= 95% parity on your precision/recall bar for high-risk classes.
- Primary workloads: short structured prompts (transaction attributes), free-text dispute summaries, and a 1–3 step multi-turn assistant used by ops.
- Key constraints: latency SLO < 200ms p50 for single-turn classification; throughput ~300 QPS at peak; SOC2 controls + data residency in us-west.

Recommended evaluation plan (next 2 weeks)
1) We’ll run a 2k-sample promptset from your repo (attached: paygrid_eval_promptset.csv) across 3 open models + your current proprietary baseline for parity testing.
2) Metrics: class-wise precision/recall/F1, confusion matrices for high-risk labels, latency p50/p95, and token cost. We’ll also include a pragmatic human eval for edge cases.
3) Acceptance thresholds: initial pass target is +/-5% relative F1 vs baseline for core labels. For high-risk labels we propose stricter +/-2% threshold — open to your inputs.
4) Deliverables: benchmark PDF (will include per-prompt examples and failure modes), recommended model(s) and quantization profile, and a mutual action plan for a 6-week pilot.

Attachments: paygrid_eval_promptset.csv; I’ll upload interim benchmark results to the drive link and share once the run completes.

Ask: please confirm the acceptance thresholds above and that we can run the attached promptset (it only contains anonymized examples). If procurement needs to be looped now, I can add them to the MAP doc.

Next steps
- You: confirm thresholds + approve run (Samir)
- Us: run the benchmark across chosen models, share results and a short demo week of Feb 23–27
- Schedule: reserve a 30-min review on Feb 24 — propose 9–9:30am PT.

Thanks — excited to dig in.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0182

From: Samir Khan <samir@paygrid.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Laura Chen <laura.chen@paygrid.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 16 Feb 2026 08:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call: model fit & evaluation plan for PayGrid

Thanks Marissa — this looks good and pragmatic. A few clarifying points from our side:

1) Acceptance thresholds: our bar for "high-risk" labels (fraud, sanctions, AML_confirmed) needs to be no more than 1% absolute drop in F1 vs our baseline. For the other classes +/-5% sounds fine. Is +/-2% relative what you meant for high-risk, or do you prefer absolute?

2) Baselines: the proprietary baseline we referenced during the call is an ensemble (vendor X model + rule set). We'll share a snapshot export to compare exactly.

3) Cost targets: we want to understand the per-request unit economics at 300 QPS sustained for peak windows. Please include cost projections for quantized 8-bit and 4-bit profiles if you have them.

4) Data: the attached promptset looks anonymized, yes — procurement wants confirmation we won't persist raw logs in your hosted service during the benchmark. Can you confirm?

If you can answer the above, we can greenlight the run. Feb 24 at 9am PT works.

- Samir
Director of Data Science | PayGrid

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Khan <samir@paygrid.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Laura Chen <laura.chen@paygrid.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 17 Feb 2026 11:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call: model fit & evaluation plan for PayGrid

Hi all — Vivek (SE) here. Quick technical notes / suggested benchmark matrix based on the promptset Marissa shared:

Models to include (initial run)
- Llama 3 70B (open) — good baseline for instruction-following; include a 70B and 13B slice if you want cost comparisons.
- Mistral Instruct 7B (open) — strong for classification with instruction-tuning, good cost/latency tradeoff.
- Falcon 40B Instruct (open) — similar to Llama 3 on some NLU tasks, often outputs more verbose completions so we include prompt-normalization in the pipeline.
- Your proprietary baseline (vendor export) — for exact parity comparisons.

Evaluation configuration
- Quantization profiles: FP16 (baseline), int8, and 4-bit (if supported). We’ll run latency and memory profiles on a representative instance type to simulate your Dedicated setup.
- Metrics: per-class F1 with 95% bootstrap CI, latency p50/p95, token and request cost. For high-risk labels we’ll compute adversarial perturbation recall (small misspellings / obfuscated tokens).
- Acceptance thresholds: Vivek recommends absolute thresholds for clarity: high-risk labels <= 1% absolute F1 drop vs baseline; other classes <= 5% absolute drop. If that’s too strict for initial pass, we can evaluate tradeoffs and propose an incremental rollout where rules supplement model outputs for borderline cases.

Security / data handling
- For the benchmark run we can perform the evaluation inside a customer-dedicated VPC (Redwood Private) or on our hosted infra with logs redacted. For a simple parity test you can grant a temporary S3 export and we’ll consume it into an ephemeral job with no persistent logs (we will not persist raw request logs; only aggregated metrics and a small set of anonymized failure examples).

Cost projection example (rough)
- Llama 3 70B (int8): estimated $0.012 per classification at 1-token avg output; Mistral 7B (4-bit): ~$0.002 per classification. These are estimates — final depends on batching and runtime optimizations. We’ll provide precise numbers in the PDF.

Next actions (internal + external)
- Samir: confirm that absolute thresholds above are acceptable (<=1% for high-risk).
- PayGrid: provide a vendor export or confirm which baseline snapshot to use.
- Marissa / Dev: I’ll kick off the benchmark once we have sign-off and access.

Happy to jump on a quick technical pre-run call if you want to review quantization/latency tradeoffs before Feb 24.

Thanks,
Vivek Kulkarni
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
vivek@redwood.ai

From: Samir Khan <samir@paygrid.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@paygrid.com, Laura Chen <laura.chen@paygrid.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 09:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call: model fit & evaluation plan for PayGrid

Appreciate the details, Vivek. We’re comfortable with the absolute thresholds you proposed (<=1% absolute for high-risk; <=5% for others) and procurement is ok with the ephemeral data flow as described (procurement loop copied).

We’ll upload the vendor export to the drive folder by EOD today and confirm the 30-min review on Feb 24 at 9am PT. Please include the cost projection table in the benchmark PDF and a short section on failure modes and suggested fallback rules for any high-risk class misses.

See you on the 24th — Samir
